# Nature-inspired algorithms — function ontology

**Card 13 · source workbook `ontology/xlsx/Nature_Algorithms_Ontology_v1.xlsx` · generated by `scripts/build-knowledge.js` — do not edit by hand.**

## Scope boundary

How biological populations search, decide, route, allocate and adapt, and which of those transfer to computational method. Use for search, optimisation, routing, scheduling, allocation, anomaly detection and distributed coordination. WARNING — metaphor inflation is the standing failure mode of this field: a large share of published nature-inspired algorithms are renamed variants of existing methods with a new animal attached, and novelty of metaphor is not novelty of mechanism. Before proposing one, state what the algorithm does that a standard method does not, and prefer the established named method over its rebranded variant. Where the workbook flags this, carry the flag through.

## Challenge triggers

| Challenge | Prioritise | Reasoning rule |
|---|---|---|
| Black-box global optimization, no gradients, expensive structure | A1 (or CMA-ES variant) | If the landscape is opaque, buy information with a population, not a single trajectory |
| Combinatorial routing / graph tour (TSP, VRP) | A2 | Exploit graph locality: reinforce edges that recur in good tours |
| Continuous parameter tuning, moderate dimensions | A3 | Share best-known positions socially; keep inertia for exploration |
| Optimum drifts over time (dynamic optimization) | A2 (P-ACO/immigrants) or multi-swar… | Keep memory of past environments AND standing diversity; balance transfer vs forgetting |
| Anomaly / novelty detection without labeled attacks | A4 | Learn the shape of normal; flag what fails censorship against it; keep memory of past anomalies |
| Design a spatial network balancing cost, efficiency, resilience | A8 | Grow with redundancy, prune by real flow, keep loops that pay for themselves in fault tolerance |
| Coordinate many cheap/unreliable robots for coverage or construct… | A12 | Move intelligence into interaction rules and the environment, not into individuals |
| Form / regenerate a global shape with identical simple units | A11 + A12 (Turing-driven motion) | Emergent (principle-2) patterning is robust & self-healing but limited to pattern families |
| Generate organic branching structures procedurally | A14 | Write the growth program, not the geometry; randomize parameters for natural variation |
| Escape local optima in scheduling/placement with natural neighbor… | A6 | Accept uphill moves early under a cooling budget |
| Associative recall / content-addressable memory | A5 | Store in weights via local correlation; recall by relaxation from partial cue |
| Evaluate a shiny 'novel' bio-metaphor algorithm | Sörensen checklist first | Demand: component-level novelty vs PSO/DE/GA, standard benchmark suites, tuned baselines, statistical tests |

## Algorithm families

The baseline column is the antidote to metaphor inflation. If the classical baseline already solves it, say so.

| Family | Members | Core contribution | Honest classical baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Evolutionary computation | A1 (GA, ES/CMA-ES, GP, DE, NEAT) | Population search of encodable design spaces | Gradient methods where gradients exist; Bayesian optimization for expensive evals |
| Swarm intelligence (optimization) | A2 ACO, A3 PSO, A15 ABC, A9 BFO, (A16 FA — disputed) | Shared-memory / social amplification of good solutions | LKH & exact solvers (routing); CMA-ES/DE (continuous) |
| Stigmergic & collective systems | A10 Stigmergy, A12 Swarm robotics | Coordination without communication or reliability of individuals | Centralized planners when comms & positioning are available |
| Developmental / morphogenetic | A11 RD, A13 GRN, A14 L-systems, A7 CA | Growth, pattern, self-repair of structure from local rules | Direct geometric specification / top-down assembly (Rubenstein 2014) |
| Immune & learning systems | A4 AIS, A5 Hebbian | Adaptive detection & memory from local rules | Modern statistical ML / deep learning |
| Physical-process analogues | A6 SA (physics, flagged) | Barrier crossing via controlled randomness | Tabu search; ILP where tractable |

## Maturity guide

- **Item** — Guidance
- **Why it was added** — 'Reference implementation' says what exists. It does not say whether anyone should rely on it. This column does.
- **Level 1 — research-only** — Published papers and lab/simulation demos only. No independent competitive benchmark record, no maintained tooling. Examples: A13 morphogenetic engineering, A8 slime-mold design, A16 FA.
- **Level 2 — benchmarked competitive** — Independent studies on STANDARD suites (BBOB/CEC/TSPLIB/MPB) show it competitive with tuned baselines. Examples: A2 ACO (MMAS), A15 ABC, A9 BFO (dynamic settings).
- **Level 3 — used in industry tooling** — Named commercial/industrial tools employ it (name WHICH). Examples: A12/Reynolds boids in VFX & game crowd tooling; Kilobot platform manufactured for research market; EC uses documented in Eiben & Smith 2015.
- **Level 4 — standard library available** — Maintained mainstream library ships it: SciPy (dual_annealing, differential_evolution), MATLAB Global Optimization Toolbox (ga, particleswarm, simulannealbnd), pycma, DEAP, NEAT-Python, Houdini L-System node, NEST/Brian…
- **Evidence rule** — Cite the concrete artifact (library name / product / benchmark study). If you cannot, the level is research-only and the row is marked [estimated].
- **Direction of error** — When in doubt, rate LOWER. Overstating maturity is the field's characteristic sin.
- **METAPHOR-INFLATION CAVEAT (required reading)** — This field has produced hundreds of shallow 'novel-metaphor' algorithms. Sörensen (2015, ITOR, DOI 10.1111/itor.12001) exposes the pattern; Camacho-Villalón, Dorigo & Stützle (ITOR 2023) prove six famous ones (grey wolf…
- **Interaction with adoption blockers** — 'Adoption blocker' column values are restricted to: compute cost / convergence guarantees / benchmark inferiority vs classical methods / metaphor-without-mechanism / hardware gap / verification of emergence.
